intro: Hi! In this lesson you learn to build new words from words you already know: happy → unhappy, pay → payment, use → useful and useless. You also meet word families like decide, decision and decisive, and learn the trick to tell which form a sentence needs. Warm-up: what's one big decision you made this year?
teachingNotes: Prefixes (awalan, a piece at the FRONT of a word) change the meaning but not the kind of word: un- and dis- = not / the opposite (unhappy, unusual, unemployed, unfriendly, unhealthy, unfair, unlucky; dishonest, disagree, dislike, disappear, dissatisfied), re- = again (redo, rewrite, rebuild, reopen, restart, reuse). The hard part: there is NO rule for un- vs dis-; it must be learnt word by word. Common error: *'He is very unhonest' → dishonest. If a learner must guess, un- is the more common one, but tell them to check a dictionary. Also: not every word starting with re- is re + word (read, remember, report, return, repair): don't let learners split them. With a few verbs un- reverses an action (unlock, unpack): only if asked.

in-/im- (incorrect, informal, independent, inexpensive; impossible, impolite, impatient) are a NOTE only: im- usually before p or m. Don't test them, and don't teach il-/ir-/non- unless asked. inexpensive = murah (not mahal). Indonesian says 'tidak jujur' as two words; English joins the 'not' into one word (dishonest), and Indonesian ke-tidak-an (ketidakjujuran) is the closest analogy.

Suffixes (akhiran, a piece at the END) usually change the kind of word. -er/-or = a person who does it (teacher, driver, manager, employer; visitor, actor, director): mostly -er, learn the -or words; -er can also be a machine (computer, printer, charger). -tion/-sion and -ment make nouns from verbs (inform → information, invite → invitation, explain → explanation, decide → decision, discuss → discussion; pay → payment, develop → development, agree → agreement, improve → improvement). Point out spelling changes (decide → decision, explain → explanation, not 'explaination') and stress: the syllable before -tion/-sion is stressed (in-for-MA-tion, de-CI-sion). -ful = with/full of, -less = without (useful/useless, careful/careless, helpful/helpless, hopeful/hopeless): -ful has ONE l ('usefull' ✗), but the adverb has two (carefully, successfully). Not every -ful word has a -less partner (beautiful, successful → unsuccessful), and priceless = sangat berharga (not 'tanpa harga'); careless = ceroboh.

Word families: decide / decision / decisive (tegas); succeed / success / successful / successfully; employ / employer (pemberi kerja) / employee (karyawan, -ee = the person who receives the action, stress em-ploy-EE) / employment / unemployed. The KEY skill is choosing the form from the slot: after a/an/the/my/this (with nothing after the gap) → noun; after be or very/so/too/really, or before a noun → adjective (a successful business: the noun after the gap decides); after a verb (+ object) → adverb (finished the project successfully); after to/can/will/don't or a subject → verb (I can't decide). Common errors: *'I made a decide' → a decision; *'The event was very success' → successful. Indonesian has a similar system: putus → memutuskan (verb), keputusan (ke-an, noun); kerja → bekerja, pekerja (pe-, the person, like -er), pekerjaan (pe-an, noun).

Collocations to keep natural: make a decision (British also 'take a decision': accept it), make a payment, give information (uncountable: no 'informations', no 'an information'), have a discussion. Don't test economic/economical-type pairs or words with two correct forms for one gap.

Limits: A0–A2 grammar only (present and past simple, present continuous, present perfect with ever/never/just/already/yet, will, going to, can/could, should/have to, comparatives). No passive (avoid 'was rebuilt', 'is cancelled'), no relative clauses (say 'teacher = teach + -er', not 'a person who teaches'), no past perfect, reported speech or second conditional. Don't teach -ness, -ity, -able, -ous, -ise/-ize, -al or other prefixes (mis-, pre-, over-) unless the learner asks.

keyPoints.title: Prefixes: un-, dis- and re-
keyPoints.explanation: A prefix goes at the front of a word and changes the meaning, not the kind of word. un- and dis- mean not or the opposite: unhappy, unusual, unemployed; dishonest, disagree, dislike. There's no rule for un- or dis-: learn each word ('unhonest' is wrong). re- means again: redo, rewrite, rebuild. Note: in-/im- also mean not (incorrect, impossible).

examples.en: My cousin is unemployed. He's looking for a job in Jakarta.
examples.id: Sepupu saya menganggur. Dia sedang mencari kerja di Jakarta.
Saya tidak suka kerja di hari Sabtu.

examples.en: My manager didn't like the slides, so I had to redo them.
examples.id: Atasan saya tidak suka slide-nya, jadi saya harus membuatnya ulang.

id.title: Prefix (awalan): un-, dis- dan re-
id.explanation: Prefix (awalan) ditaruh di depan kata dan mengubah artinya, bukan jenis katanya. un- dan dis- artinya tidak atau kebalikannya: unhappy (tidak bahagia), unusual (tidak biasa), unemployed (menganggur); dishonest (tidak jujur), disagree (tidak setuju), dislike (tidak suka). Tidak ada aturan kapan un- dan kapan dis-: hafalkan per kata ('unhonest' salah). re- artinya lagi / ulang: redo, rewrite, rebuild. Catatan: in-/im- juga berarti tidak (incorrect, impossible).

keyPoints.title: Suffixes: -er/-or, -tion/-sion, -ment, -ful and -less
keyPoints.explanation: A suffix goes at the end and usually changes the kind of word. -er/-or makes a person (teacher, visitor). -tion/-sion and -ment make a noun from a verb (inform → information, decide → decision, pay → payment, develop → development). -ful means with or full of, -less means without: useful / useless, careful / careless. -ful has only one l.

examples.en: The museum had a lot of visitors last weekend.
examples.id: Museum itu punya banyak pengunjung akhir pekan lalu.

examples.en: You can make the payment by bank transfer.
examples.id: Kamu bisa melakukan pembayaran lewat transfer bank.

examples.en: Without Wi-Fi, this app is useless.
examples.id: Tanpa Wi-Fi, aplikasi ini tidak berguna.

id.title: Suffix (akhiran): -er/-or, -tion/-sion, -ment, -ful dan -less
id.explanation: Suffix (akhiran) ditaruh di belakang kata dan biasanya mengubah jenis katanya. -er/-or membuat kata untuk orang (teacher, visitor). -tion/-sion dan -ment membuat kata benda dari kata kerja (inform → information, decide → decision, pay → payment, develop → development). -ful artinya punya / penuh, -less artinya tanpa: useful (berguna) / useless (tidak berguna), careful (hati-hati) / careless (ceroboh). -ful hanya pakai satu l.

keyPoints.title: Word families and the right form for the gap
keyPoints.explanation: Many words come in families: decide (verb) / decision (noun) / decisive (adjective); succeed / success / successful / successfully; employ / employer / employee / employment. The sentence tells you which form you need: after a/the/my → a noun (a decision); after be or very, or before a noun → an adjective (very successful, a successful business); after a verb → an adverb (finished successfully); after to/can/don't → a verb (I can't decide).

examples.en: We have to make a decision before Friday.
examples.id: Kita harus membuat keputusan sebelum hari Jumat.

examples.en: Her online shop is very successful.
The company has two hundred employees.
examples.id: Perusahaan itu punya dua ratus karyawan.

id.title: Keluarga kata dan bentuk yang tepat untuk titik-titiknya
id.explanation: Banyak kata punya keluarga: decide (kata kerja, memutuskan) / decision (kata benda, keputusan) / decisive (kata sifat, tegas); succeed / success / successful / successfully; employ / employer / employee / employment. Kalimatnya memberi tahu bentuk mana yang dibutuhkan: setelah a/the/my → kata benda (a decision); setelah be atau very, atau sebelum kata benda → kata sifat (very successful, a successful business); setelah kata kerja → adverb (finished successfully); setelah to/can/don't → kata kerja (I can't decide).

guidedPractice.prompt: Make the opposite with un- or dis-: Rina never drinks coffee. She ___ (likes) the taste.
guidedPractice.hint: like takes dis-, not un-. Rina = she, so keep the -s.

guidedPractice.prompt: Add re- to the word in brackets: The shop near my kos is closed for a week. It ___ (opens) next Monday.
Complete with -ful or -less: Budi often loses his keys and his phone. He's very ___ (care).
guidedPractice.hint: Losing things = no care. -less means without.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make a noun from the word in brackets: Can you give me some ___ (inform) about the English course?
guidedPractice.hint: After some you need a noun. inform + -ation.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake: The event was very success.
guidedPractice.hint: After very you need an adjective: success + -ful.

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about a decision you made this year. Use decision or decide.
independentPractice.hint: This year I made a decision: I ... / I decided to ...

independentPractice.prompt: What's one thing you dislike about your city? Write one sentence.
independentPractice.hint: I dislike the traffic in ... because ...

independentPractice.prompt: Which app is really useful for you, and why? Write one sentence.
independentPractice.hint: ... is really useful because it helps me ...

assessment.prompt: Make the opposite of the word in brackets with un-, dis- or re-: I'm sorry, but I ___ (agree) with you. I think the plan is too expensive.
assessment.rubric: Correct: disagree (agree takes dis-). 'unagree' = 30 (right idea, wrong prefix: un- or dis- must be learnt word by word). 'don't agree' = 50 (right meaning, but the task asks for the prefix form). 'agree' or 'reagree' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Add un-, dis- or re- to the word in brackets: My laptop crashed before I saved the report, so now I have to ___ (write) it.
assessment.rubric: Correct: rewrite (re- = again). 'write' = 30 (no prefix: the point is writing it again). 'unwrite' or 'diswrite' = 0. 're-write' = 90.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Our ___ (visit) from Japan is waiting in the lobby. Can you take him to the meeting room?
assessment.rubric: Correct: visitor (a person: visit + -or). 'visiter' = 70 (right idea, but this word ends in -or). 'visitors' = 60 (one person: him). 'visit' or 'visiting' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the word in brackets + -ful or -less: This charger doesn't work with any of my phones. It's completely ___ (use).
assessment.rubric: Correct: useless (-less = without: no use). 'usless' = 80 (spelling). 'useful' or 'usefull' = 0 (the opposite meaning).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: After a long talk with her parents, Sari made a ___ (decide): she's going to study in Bandung.
assessment.rubric: Correct: decision (after 'a' with nothing after the gap you need a noun: decide → decision). 'decission' or 'desicion' = 80 (spelling). 'decide' = 0 (a verb can't follow 'a'). 'decisive' = 20 (adjective).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Dimas finished the project ___ (success), and his manager was very happy.
assessment.rubric: Correct: successfully (it says how he finished: after a verb + object you need an adverb, -ly). 'successfuly' = 80 (spelling: two l's). 'successful' = 30 (adjective, not adverb). 'success' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Pak Hasan has a small printing company in Bogor. He pays his twelve ___ (employ) every Friday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: employees (the people who work for him: employ + -ee, plural after twelve). 'employee' = 70 (no plural -s). 'employers' = 20 (an employer is the boss, the one who pays). 'employment' = 0.

blocks.text:
A **prefix** is a small piece at the **front** of a word. It changes the **meaning**, but the kind of word stays the same: *happy* is an adjective (a describing word) and *unhappy* is an adjective too; *like* is a verb (an action word) and *dislike* is a verb too.
- **un-** = not: *happy → **un**happy, usual → **un**usual, employed → **un**employed* (menganggur), *friendly → **un**friendly*
- **dis-** = not / the opposite: *honest → **dis**honest, agree → **dis**agree, like → **dis**like, appear → **dis**appear* (menghilang)
- **re-** = again: *do → **re**do, write → **re**write, build → **re**build, open → **re**open*

Indonesian puts *tidak* before the word as a separate word (*tidak jujur*). English joins the 'not' to the word: ***dis**honest*, one word.

id.text:
**Prefix** (awalan) adalah potongan kecil di **depan** kata. Prefix mengubah **arti**, tapi jenis katanya tetap: *happy* kata sifat (kata yang menjelaskan) dan *unhappy* juga kata sifat; *like* kata kerja (kata tindakan) dan *dislike* juga kata kerja.
- **un-** = tidak: *happy → **un**happy* (tidak bahagia), *usual → **un**usual* (tidak biasa), *employed → **un**employed* (menganggur), *friendly → **un**friendly* (tidak ramah)
- **dis-** = tidak / kebalikannya: *honest → **dis**honest* (tidak jujur), *agree → **dis**agree* (tidak setuju), *like → **dis**like* (tidak suka), *appear → **dis**appear* (menghilang)
- **re-** = lagi, ulang: *do → **re**do* (mengerjakan ulang), *write → **re**write* (menulis ulang), *build → **re**build* (membangun kembali), *open → **re**open* (buka lagi)

Bahasa Indonesia menaruh *tidak* sebagai kata terpisah (*tidak jujur*). Bahasa Inggris menggabungkan 'tidak' itu ke katanya: ***dis**honest*, satu kata.

rows.en: Sari was unhappy with her old job.

blocks.text: **Not every re- word is re + word.** In *read, remember, report, return* and *repair*, the 're' is just part of the word: *remember* doesn't mean 'member again'. **re-** means *again* only when the rest is a real word with a related meaning: *re**open*** = open again, *re**build*** = build again.

id.text: **Tidak semua kata yang diawali re- itu re + kata.** Di *read, remember, report, return* dan *repair*, 're' hanya bagian dari katanya: *remember* (ingat) bukan berarti 'member lagi'. **re-** berarti *lagi / ulang* hanya kalau sisanya kata asli yang artinya berhubungan: *re**open*** = buka lagi, *re**build*** = bangun lagi.

blocks.prompt: After the flood, the village needed to ___ its school.
blocks.explain: The school was damaged, so they build it again: re- = again, rebuild. 'unbuild' and 'disbuild' are not English words.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: After the flood, the village needed to ___ its school.
id.explain: Sekolahnya rusak, jadi dibangun lagi: re- = lagi, rebuild. 'unbuild' dan 'disbuild' bukan kata bahasa Inggris.

material.title: un- or dis-? Learn them word by word

id.title: un- atau dis-? Hafalkan per kata

blocks.text:
Here's the hard part: **there is no rule** that tells you when to use **un-** and when to use **dis-**. Both mean *not*. You simply learn each word with its prefix, like you learn the word itself. That's why learners say 'unhonest': it sounds logical, but the real word is **dishonest**.

The common ones:
- **un-**: *unhappy, unusual, unemployed, unfriendly, unhealthy, unfair, unlucky, unclear, uncomfortable, unsuccessful*
- **dis-**: *dishonest, disagree, dislike, disappear, dissatisfied, disadvantage*

**un-** is the more common prefix, so it's the better guess when you don't know, but check a dictionary before you use a new word. Note *dissatisfied* has **double s**: dis + satisfied.

id.text:
Ini bagian yang sulit: **tidak ada aturan** yang memberi tahu kapan pakai **un-** dan kapan pakai **dis-**. Dua-duanya berarti *tidak*. Kamu hafalkan setiap kata bersama prefix-nya, sama seperti kamu menghafal katanya. Karena itu banyak orang bilang 'unhonest': kedengarannya logis, tapi kata yang benar adalah **dishonest**.

Yang sering dipakai:
- **un-**: *unhappy* (tidak bahagia), *unusual* (tidak biasa), *unemployed* (menganggur), *unfriendly* (tidak ramah), *unhealthy* (tidak sehat), *unfair* (tidak adil), *unlucky* (sial), *unclear* (tidak jelas), *uncomfortable* (tidak nyaman), *unsuccessful* (tidak berhasil)
- **dis-**: *dishonest* (tidak jujur), *disagree* (tidak setuju), *dislike* (tidak suka), *disappear* (menghilang), *dissatisfied* (tidak puas), *disadvantage* (kerugian, kekurangan)

**un-** lebih sering dipakai, jadi itu tebakan yang lebih aman kalau kamu tidak tahu, tapi cek kamus dulu sebelum memakai kata baru. Perhatikan *dissatisfied* pakai **s ganda**: dis + satisfied.

rows.en: He's very dishonest.
rows.id: Dia sangat tidak jujur.

rows.en: It's unusual to see Budi in the office on Sunday.
rows.id: Jarang sekali melihat Budi di kantor hari Minggu.

rows.en: Many customers were dissatisfied with the delivery.
rows.id: Banyak pelanggan tidak puas dengan pengirimannya.

rows.en: This chair is really uncomfortable.
rows.id: Kursi ini benar-benar tidak nyaman.

blocks.text: **A note on in- and im-.** These also mean *not*: ***in**correct, **in**formal, **in**expensive* (murah, not mahal!), ***im**possible, **im**polite, **im**patient*. **im-** usually comes before **p** or **m**, because it's easier to say. Just recognise them for now; this lesson practises un-, dis- and re-.

id.text: **Catatan tentang in- dan im-.** Dua-duanya juga berarti *tidak*: ***in**correct* (tidak benar), ***in**formal* (tidak resmi), ***in**expensive* (murah, bukan mahal!), ***im**possible* (tidak mungkin), ***im**polite* (tidak sopan), ***im**patient* (tidak sabar). **im-** biasanya dipakai sebelum **p** atau **m**, karena lebih mudah diucapkan. Untuk sekarang cukup kenali saja; pelajaran ini melatih un-, dis- dan re-.

blocks.prompt: My brother lost his job in May, so now he's ___.
blocks.explain: employed takes un-: unemployed (menganggur). There's no rule for un- or dis-, so this one is learnt as a word. 'disemployed' and 'inemployed' don't exist.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: My brother lost his job in May, so now he's ___.
id.explain: employed memakai un-: unemployed (menganggur). Tidak ada aturan untuk un- atau dis-, jadi kata ini dihafal saja. 'disemployed' dan 'inemployed' tidak ada.

blocks.text:
A **suffix** is a small piece at the **end** of a word. Unlike a prefix, it usually changes the **kind** of word.
- **-er / -or** = the person doing it: *teach → teach**er**, drive → driv**er**, manage → manag**er**; visit → visit**or**, act → act**or**, direct → direct**or***. Most words take **-er**; the **-or** words just have to be learnt. **-er** can also be a machine: *comput**er**, print**er**, charg**er***.
- **-tion / -sion** make a **noun** (a thing word) from a verb (an action word): *inform → inform**ation**, invite → invit**ation**, decide → deci**sion**, discuss → discuss**ion***.
- **-ment** also makes a noun from a verb: *pay → pay**ment**, develop → develop**ment**, agree → agree**ment**, improve → improve**ment***.

Indonesian does the same with *pe-*: *kerja → **pe**kerja* (the person, like -er) and *pe-an*: *bayar → **pem**bayar**an*** (the thing, like -ment).

id.text:
**Suffix** (akhiran) adalah potongan kecil di **belakang** kata. Berbeda dengan prefix, suffix biasanya mengubah **jenis** kata.
- **-er / -or** = orang yang melakukannya: *teach → teach**er*** (guru), *drive → driv**er*** (sopir), *manage → manag**er*** (manajer); *visit → visit**or*** (tamu, pengunjung), *act → act**or*** (aktor), *direct → direct**or*** (direktur, sutradara). Kebanyakan kata pakai **-er**; kata dengan **-or** harus dihafal. **-er** juga bisa berarti alat: *comput**er**, print**er**, charg**er***.
- **-tion / -sion** membuat **kata benda** (kata untuk benda/hal) dari kata kerja (kata tindakan): *inform → inform**ation*** (informasi), *invite → invit**ation*** (undangan), *decide → deci**sion*** (keputusan), *discuss → discuss**ion*** (diskusi).
- **-ment** juga membuat kata benda dari kata kerja: *pay → pay**ment*** (pembayaran), *develop → develop**ment*** (perkembangan, pembangunan), *agree → agree**ment*** (kesepakatan), *improve → improve**ment*** (perbaikan).

Bahasa Indonesia juga begitu dengan *pe-*: *kerja → **pe**kerja* (orangnya, seperti -er) dan *pe-an*: *bayar → **pem**bayar**an*** (bendanya, seperti -ment).

rows.en: Thanks for the invitation to your wedding!

blocks.text: **Spelling and sound.** The spelling often changes a little: *decide → decision, explain → explanation* (no i: not 'explaination'), *invite → invitation*. **-tion** sounds like 'syen', and the stress (the strong part) falls just before it: *in-for-MA-tion, in-vi-TA-tion, de-CI-sion*. And **information** has no -s and no *an*: *some information*, never 'informations'.

id.text: **Ejaan dan bunyi.** Ejaannya sering berubah sedikit: *decide → decision, explain → explanation* (tanpa i: bukan 'explaination'), *invite → invitation*. **-tion** dibaca seperti 'syen', dan tekanannya (bagian yang diucapkan paling kuat) jatuh tepat sebelumnya: *in-for-MA-tion, in-vi-TA-tion, de-CI-sion*. Dan **information** tidak pakai -s dan tidak pakai *an*: *some information*, bukan 'informations'.

blocks.prompt: Thanks for the ___. Now I understand how the app works.
blocks.explain: After 'the' you need a noun: explain → explanation. 'explain' is the verb, and 'explaination' is a spelling mistake (the i goes away).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Thanks for the ___. Now I understand how the app works.
id.explain: Setelah 'the' kamu butuh kata benda: explain → explanation (penjelasan). 'explain' adalah kata kerja, dan 'explaination' salah ejaan (huruf i-nya hilang).

blocks.text:
**-ful** and **-less** make **adjectives** (describing words) from nouns.
- **-ful** = with, full of: *use → use**ful*** (berguna), *care → care**ful*** (hati-hati), *help → help**ful*** (membantu), *success → success**ful*** (sukses)
- **-less** = without: *use → use**less*** (tidak berguna), *care → care**less*** (ceroboh), *help → help**less*** (tidak berdaya), *home → home**less*** (tunawisma), *cash → cash**less*** (nontunai)

So **useful** and **useless** are opposites, and so are **careful** and **careless**.

**Spelling:** the suffix **-ful** has only **one l**, even though the word *full* has two: *useful*, never 'usefull'. When you add **-ly** to make an adverb (a word for *how* you do something), you get two l's: *careful → careful**ly***, *successful → successful**ly***.

id.text:
**-ful** dan **-less** membuat **kata sifat** (kata yang menjelaskan) dari kata benda.
- **-ful** = dengan, penuh: *use → use**ful*** (berguna), *care → care**ful*** (hati-hati), *help → help**ful*** (membantu), *success → success**ful*** (sukses)
- **-less** = tanpa: *use → use**less*** (tidak berguna), *care → care**less*** (ceroboh), *help → help**less*** (tidak berdaya), *home → home**less*** (tunawisma), *cash → cash**less*** (nontunai)

Jadi **useful** dan **useless** berlawanan, begitu juga **careful** dan **careless**.

**Ejaan:** akhiran **-ful** hanya pakai **satu l**, walaupun kata *full* (penuh) pakai dua: *useful*, bukan 'usefull'. Kalau kamu menambah **-ly** untuk membuat adverb (kata yang menjelaskan *bagaimana* sesuatu dilakukan), hasilnya dua l: *careful → careful**ly***, *successful → successful**ly***.

blocks.text: **Not every -ful word has a -less partner.** *beautiful* has no 'beautiless', and the opposite of *successful* is ***un**successful*, not 'successless'. And one surprise: **priceless** means *sangat berharga* (so valuable you can't put a price on it), not 'tanpa harga' or 'gratis'. Free = **free**.

id.text: **Tidak semua kata -ful punya pasangan -less.** *beautiful* tidak punya 'beautiless', dan lawan *successful* adalah ***un**successful*, bukan 'successless'. Dan satu kejutan: **priceless** artinya *sangat berharga* (saking berharganya tidak bisa diberi harga), bukan 'tanpa harga' atau 'gratis'. Gratis = **free**.

blocks.prompt: Be ___ with that box. There are glasses inside.
blocks.explain: Glasses can break, so you need care: -ful = with, careful. careless (ceroboh) is the opposite, and 'carefull' has one l too many.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Be ___ with that box. There are glasses inside.
id.explain: Gelas bisa pecah, jadi harus hati-hati: -ful = dengan, careful. careless (ceroboh) artinya kebalikannya, dan 'carefull' kelebihan satu l.

material.title: Word families: which form does the sentence need?

id.title: Keluarga kata: bentuk mana yang dibutuhkan kalimatnya?

blocks.text:
A **word family** is a group of words from the same root:
- **decide** (verb) / **decision** (noun) / **decisive** (adjective: tegas, quick to decide)
- **succeed** (verb) / **success** (noun) / **successful** (adjective) / **successfully** (adverb)
- **employ** (verb: mempekerjakan) / **employer** (the boss or company) / **employee** (karyawan) / **employment** (noun) / **unemployed** (adjective)

Indonesian has the same idea: *putus → **mem**utus**kan*** (verb, like *decide*), ***ke**putus**an*** (noun, like *decision*); *kerja → **be**kerja, **pe**kerja, **pe**kerja**an***.

**The key skill: look at the words around the gap.**
- after **a / an / the / my / this**, with nothing after the gap → a **noun**: *I made a **decision**.*
- after **be** (is, are, was) or **very / so / too / really** → an **adjective**: *The event was very **successful**.*
- **before a noun** → an **adjective**, even after *a*: *a **successful** business* (the noun *business* comes after the gap)
- after a **verb** (and its object), saying *how* → an **adverb**: *She passed the test **successfully**.*
- after **to / can / will / don't**, or after the person → a **verb**: *I can't **decide**.*

id.text:
**Keluarga kata** (word family) adalah kelompok kata dari kata dasar yang sama:
- **decide** (kata kerja: memutuskan) / **decision** (kata benda: keputusan) / **decisive** (kata sifat: tegas, cepat memutuskan)
- **succeed** (kata kerja: berhasil) / **success** (kata benda: kesuksesan) / **successful** (kata sifat: sukses) / **successfully** (adverb: dengan sukses)
- **employ** (kata kerja: mempekerjakan) / **employer** (atasan atau perusahaan, pemberi kerja) / **employee** (karyawan) / **employment** (kata benda: pekerjaan, lapangan kerja) / **unemployed** (kata sifat: menganggur)

Bahasa Indonesia punya ide yang sama: *putus → **mem**utus**kan*** (kata kerja, seperti *decide*), ***ke**putus**an*** (kata benda, seperti *decision*); *kerja → **be**kerja, **pe**kerja, **pe**kerja**an***.

**Keterampilan kuncinya: lihat kata-kata di sekitar titik-titik.**
- setelah **a / an / the / my / this**, dan tidak ada kata benda sesudahnya → **kata benda**: *I made a **decision**.*
- setelah **be** (is, are, was) atau **very / so / too / really** → **kata sifat**: *The event was very **successful**.*
- **sebelum kata benda** → **kata sifat**, walaupun setelah *a*: *a **successful** business* (kata benda *business* ada sesudah titik-titik)
- setelah **kata kerja** (dan objeknya), menjelaskan *bagaimana* → **adverb**: *She passed the test **successfully**.*
- setelah **to / can / will / don't**, atau setelah orangnya → **kata kerja**: *I can't **decide**.*

rows.en: We have to make a decision before Friday.
rows.id: Kita harus membuat keputusan sebelum hari Jumat.

id.note: a + ___ (tidak ada kata sesudahnya) → kata benda

rows.en: My sister runs a successful online shop.
rows.id: Kakak saya punya toko online yang sukses.

rows.en: I want to succeed in my new job.
rows.id: Saya ingin berhasil di pekerjaan baru saya.

rows.en: The company has two hundred employees.
rows.id: Perusahaan itu punya dua ratus karyawan.

rows.en: Good employers pay their staff on time.
rows.id: Pemberi kerja yang baik membayar stafnya tepat waktu.

blocks.text: **The two common mistakes.** 'I made a decide' → after *a* you need the noun: *a **decision***. 'The event was very success' → after *very* you need the adjective: *very **successful***. And watch **employer** vs **employee**: the employ**er** gives the job and pays; the employ**ee** (stress at the end: em-ploy-EE) does the job and gets paid.

id.text: **Dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi.** 'I made a decide' → setelah *a* kamu butuh kata benda: *a **decision***. 'The event was very success' → setelah *very* kamu butuh kata sifat: *very **successful***. Dan hati-hati dengan **employer** dan **employee**: employ**er** memberi pekerjaan dan membayar; employ**ee** (tekanan di akhir: em-ploy-II) mengerjakan pekerjaannya dan dibayar.

blocks.prompt: I'm not sure. I can't ___ which laptop to buy.
blocks.explain: After can't you need a verb: decide. decision is a noun (a thing) and decisive is an adjective (tegas).

id.prompt: Lengkapi: I'm not sure. I can't ___ which laptop to buy.
id.explain: Setelah can't kamu butuh kata kerja: decide. decision adalah kata benda dan decisive adalah kata sifat (tegas).

suggestedQuestions: How do I know if a word takes un- or dis-?
What's the difference between employer and employee?
Why is it 'useful' with one l but 'carefully' with two?
How can I tell if a gap needs a noun or an adjective?

flashcards.back: The event was very successful. (very + adjective)

resources.title: How to change a verb into a noun!
resources.note: An intermediate lesson by Ronnie on making nouns from verbs with -ment and -ion (payment, information), with a quiz on engVid.

id.note: Pelajaran tingkat menengah dari Ronnie tentang membuat kata benda dari kata kerja dengan -ment dan -ion (payment, information), dengan kuis di engVid.

id.intro: Hai! Di pelajaran ini kamu belajar membuat kata baru dari kata yang sudah kamu tahu: happy → unhappy, pay → payment, use → useful dan useless. Kamu juga mengenal keluarga kata seperti decide, decision dan decisive, dan belajar triknya untuk tahu bentuk mana yang dibutuhkan kalimat. Pemanasan: apa satu keputusan besar yang kamu buat tahun ini?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana aku tahu sebuah kata pakai un- atau dis-?
Kenapa 'useful' pakai satu l tapi 'carefully' pakai dua?
Bagaimana cara tahu titik-titiknya butuh kata benda atau kata sifat?

assessment.wf-1: Buat lawan kata dari kata dalam kurung dengan un-, dis- atau re-: I'm sorry, but I ___ (agree) with you. I think the plan is too expensive.
assessment.wf-2: Tambahkan un-, dis- atau re- ke kata dalam kurung: My laptop crashed before I saved the report, so now I have to ___ (write) it.
assessment.wf-3: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Our ___ (visit) from Japan is waiting in the lobby. Can you take him to the meeting room?
assessment.wf-4: Lengkapi dengan kata dalam kurung + -ful atau -less: This charger doesn't work with any of my phones. It's completely ___ (use).
assessment.wf-5: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: After a long talk with her parents, Sari made a ___ (decide): she's going to study in Bandung.
assessment.wf-6: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Dimas finished the project ___ (success), and his manager was very happy.
assessment.wf-7: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Pak Hasan has a small printing company in Bogor. He pays his twelve ___ (employ) every Friday.
